summary: Jun Yang works in linguistics, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, Yang held posts as Senior Lecturer in Chinese Language at the University of Chicago and as a researcher (受託研究員) at Koyasan University.

Jundo Nagashima specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Bristol under supervisor Paul Williams, while also studying under Seitatsu Matsunami and Alexis Sanderson. Nagashima held posts at Taisho University (attested 2006, 2013–2017).

June McDaniel is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Emory University (MTS) and the University of Chicago (PhD, 1980–1986), becoming Professor of the History of Religions at the College of Charleston in 1988.

Junglan Bang specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Dongguk University and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2012) under Harunaga Isaacson, Seung-suk Jung, and Sungdoo Ahn, Bang has served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Ha completed an MA at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and a PhD at Duke University under Stanley Abe, later becoming a professor at Keimyung University.

Junjirō Takakusu (1866–1945) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku, Oxford, Leipzig, and Tokyo under Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He served as professor and president of the University of Tokyo.

Junkei Washio (1868–1941) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar educated at Toyo University. He founded Sogenkutsu in 1892 and held professorships at Toyo University and Komazawa University, as well as a post at Sendan-Rin School.

Junkichi Imanishi (b. 1935), a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served at Hokkaido University (~1969–1996), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Junko Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Matsumura studied at the Australian National University (MA, 1980) and the University of Göttingen (doctoral dissertation, 1990), and was attested as a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2011.

Junko Minamoto (b. 1947) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at Ryukoku University and Otani University (~1973–1977), later serving as a commissioned researcher (委嘱研究員) at Kansai University.

Junmai Zhang (1886–1969) worked in philosophy and sinology. He studied at Waseda University (~1906–1910), under Qichao Liang (~1906–1918), and at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1913–1915), later holding posts at Peking University (~1918–1922) and Tsinghua University.

Junsho Kato (b. 1934) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at KU Leuven and the University of Tokyo under Étienne Lamotte, Hajime Nakamura, and Akira Hirakawa, holding professorships at Nishogakusha, Nagoya, and Reitaku universities.

Juntarō Ishihama (1888–1968) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and sinology scholar who studied at Kansai University (~1905–1908). He held academic posts at Ryukoku University (~1922–1938) and Kansai University (~1924–1960).
Junzo Inagaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoshin Fukihara and held a post as section head (課長) at Otani University.

Juri Lotman (1922–1993) was a scholar in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and its Faculty of Philology between 1939 and 1961, and held a post at the University of Tartu starting in 1954.

Jurij Andreevič Smirnov (1923–1984) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (~1948–1954). In 1967, he became a scientific researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Shigeaki (Juro) Watanabe specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. A student of Gerhard Oberhammer, he held posts at the University of Tsukuba (attested 1989–1990) and as a professor at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003).
Jushu Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held academic posts as a part-time lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).
Justin Edwards Abbott (1853–1932) was a scholar in the field of Indology who studied at Dartmouth College (~1872–1876, A.B.) and at Union Theological Seminary (~1876–1879).

Justin Hartley Moore (1884–1962) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under A. V. Williams Jackson and David P. Jackson, later teaching French and Romanic languages at City College of New York.
